runtimes.name: Raw / native installation
runtimes.notes: Use the upstream installation method. HA depends on whether the product supports clustering and on externalizing state.

runtimes.name: Docker Compose
runtimes.notes: Compose is a packaging format, not a multi-host consensus system. Use Swarm or Kubernetes for multi-host scheduling.

runtimes.name: K3s
prerequisites: 3 or 5 server nodes for embedded-etcd HA
runtimes.notes: Two embedded-etcd servers do not provide a resilient quorum. Three or more server nodes are the baseline.

runtimes.name: RKE2
runtimes.notes: RKE2 server nodes are schedulable by default; separate agent nodes when workload isolation is required.

runtimes.name: Pacemaker / Corosync + STONITH
runtimes.notes: Best for active/passive systemd services and VIPs. Do not use it to fake active/active application clustering.

runtimes.name: Podman Quadlet
runtimes.notes: Quadlet is a systemd-integrated single-host lifecycle mechanism. Pair it with Pacemaker for active/passive failover.

runtimes.name: k0s
prerequisites: 3 or 5 controller nodes for etcd HA
runtimes.notes: Use controllers with etcd for HA; use workers for workload isolation and a control-plane load balancer.

runtimes.name: Docker Swarm
prerequisites: 3 or 5 manager nodes for Raft quorum
runtimes.notes: Run an odd number of managers. Two managers cannot tolerate a manager failure while preserving quorum.

runtimes.name: MicroK8s
prerequisites: 3 or 5 control-plane nodes for datastore HA
runtimes.notes: The datastore must itself be highly available; use three or more control-plane nodes for production.

solutions.name: InvenioRDM
notes: Treat the application as a distributed service; keep object storage and database outside the web process.

solutions.name: Archivematica
notes: Preservation workflows are multi-service; a single container health check is not enough.

solutions.name: Islandora
notes: Islandora is a framework/distribution; deployment must choose a Drupal/Fedora composition such as the official documentation path.

solutions.name: Fedora Repository
notes: Fedora is a repository backend, not a complete public UI; pair it with a client such as Islandora or Hyrax.

solutions.name: Samvera Hyrax
notes: Hyrax is a Rails engine and must be mounted in a host application; it is not a standalone web app.

solutions.name: RODA Community
notes: The upstream local installation guide is single-node and testing-oriented; design production storage and database separately.

solutions.name: Maarch RM
notes: The official project is hosted on Maarch Labs rather than GitHub; use the linked documentation and image registry.

solutions.name: Asalae
notes: The official source and Compose assets are hosted on the ADULLACT GitLab instance.

solutions.name: ResourceSpace
notes: Large media uploads require deliberate PHP, web-server, reverse-proxy, and filesystem limits.

solutions.name: Maarch Courrier
notes: Use the official Maarch Labs source and the current Maarch documentation; older GitHub mirrors are not authoritative.

solutions.name: Docspell
notes: The project provides Docker Compose and Helm paths; the Debian package and Helm chart are better baselines than ad-hoc source builds.

solutions.name: Nextcloud Server
notes: Use external database, Redis locking, shared or object-backed data, and a separate preview/Office strategy for HA.

solutions.name: ArchivesSpace
notes: The current technical documentation recommends Docker for new installations and documents clustering separately.

solutions.name: AtoM (Access to Memory)
notes: AtoM has official tarball, source, and Docker guidance; Elasticsearch compatibility must follow the selected AtoM release.

solutions.name: Alfresco Community Edition
notes: Alfresco Community is a multi-module platform; deploy the repository, search, Share, transforms, database, and messaging as a tested release set.

solutions.name: EPrints
notes: The official wiki distinguishes Debian/Ubuntu and RHEL/Fedora/CentOS installation paths; source Git is the production recommendation.

solutions.name: Kitodo.Production
notes: Version 4 changes the Java/Tomcat baseline; pin the server version to the selected Kitodo release.

solutions.name: Goobi workflow
notes: Goobi uses a plugin ecosystem; application, plugin, and database versions must be released as one compatibility set.

solutions.name: CollectiveAccess Providence
notes: Providence is the cataloguing application; Pawtucket is the public web layer and should be versioned separately.

solutions.name: SeedDMS
notes: The official download channel is SourceForge; GitHub mirrors are not treated as authoritative.

solutions.name: Omeka S
notes: Omeka S is intentionally extensible through modules; check module compatibility as part of the release manifest.

solutions.name: OpenKM Community
notes: The official GitHub repository is archived as of 2026; treat this adapter as maintenance-only and pin an audited release.

solutions.name: Teedy
notes: Teedy was formerly known as Sismics Docs; pin the source/release identity and avoid community images unless explicitly approved.

solutions.name: LogicalDOC Community
notes: The project publishes separate Community and Docker repositories; do not use embedded HSQLDB for production.

solutions.name: Seafile Community
notes: Current Community deployment guidance is container-first; verify the selected release's Community/Professional boundaries before applying HA automation.
